exhibition_placements.text: These colossal figures stood among the sculptures of the Mausoleum at Halikarnassos. Their scale conveys dynastic authority even though the familiar identifications as Maussollos and Artemisia remain uncertain.
At 5.78 metres high, this marble Amitābha makes the Buddha of Infinite Light an architectural presence. The surviving figure and lotus base preserve that scale despite the loss of both hands.

Turn this stone around to see two religious uses of the same material. A Buddhist figure survives on one face; an Islamic prayer niche was carved on the reverse centuries later. Damage and reuse are part of the object’s history.

Figures overlap across the shallow marble front of this sarcophagus, joining Phaedra’s story to Hippolytus’s hunt. This model records the carved front surface; the coffin’s sides and interior are outside the scan.
